title: Benchmark Refusal-Inflation x Capability Hiding: Disentangling 'Safe' From 'Can't' in Governance Numbers

original_idea.body:
# Benchmark Refusal-Inflation x Capability Hiding: Disentangling 'Safe' From 'Can't' in Governance Numbers

**Problem:** On dangerous-capability evals, a refusal counts as a low score, conflating won't with can't; governance reads low score as low capability and relaxes mitigations.

**Direction:** On an open model run a dangerous-capability proxy benchmark, re-run with benign-framing jailbreak that removes refusals, measure score gap, provide a two-axis reporting template.

**Why it matters:** Exposes a structural conflation in governance numbers. No training, single open model.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2407.14981; arXiv:2507.11544.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: refusal-inflated low scores cause governance to under-mitigate genuinely capable models; concrete misuse scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run benchmark twice with/without refusal-removal on one open model; guided and tractable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment (score-gap measurement) with clear success criterion.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Argument complicating 'safe' framing that labs are disincentivized to surface; open model.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only benchmark runs on one open model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Refusal-vs-capability conflation is discussed; the two-axis governance reporting demo may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Safety-gap/refusal-removal work exists; the governance-numbers reframing may be partly open.
